description: How an operating system virtualises the processor and memory, lets programs share safely, stores data persistently and talks to devices, learned by reading, modifying and measuring a real teaching kernel. Taught to the depth of a leading operating systems course.
modelledOn: Arpaci-Dusseau, Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
Silberschatz, Galvin and Gagne, Operating System Concepts
Tanenbaum and Bos, Modern Operating Systems
The xv6 teaching operating system and its commentary
outcomes: Explain the structure of an operating system, system calls, kernel and user modes, and the boot process.
Describe process and thread life cycles and implement and evaluate CPU scheduling algorithms.
Write correct concurrent programs with locks, semaphores, condition variables and monitors, and detect and prevent deadlock.
Analyse memory management with paging, segmentation, virtual memory and page replacement.
Explain file system design, disk scheduling, I/O subsystems and device drivers.
Describe virtual machines, multiprocessor operating systems and the design of mobile operating systems.

units.title: Introduction to operating systems
topics: What an OS does: abstraction, virtualisation, resource management, protection; history from batch to cloud and mobile
Kernel and user mode, system calls, traps and interrupts; the boot sequence
OS structures: monolithic, layered, microkernel, modules, exokernel; Linux, Windows and xv6 compared
Shell, processes and system programming in C: fork, exec, wait, pipes, signals
Building and running xv6 in an emulator; reading kernel code

units.title: Process management
topics: Processes: states, PCB, context switch, creation and termination; the process tree
Threads: user and kernel threads, pthreads, thread pools; why threads
CPU scheduling: FCFS, SJF, SRTF, priority, round robin, multilevel feedback queues; metrics and Gantt charts
Real-time scheduling (RM, EDF), proportional share and the Linux CFS
Implementing a scheduler in xv6 and measuring turnaround and response time

units.title: Concurrency and synchronisation
topics: Race conditions, critical sections, atomicity; Peterson's algorithm and hardware primitives (test-and-set, compare-and-swap)
Locks, spinlocks, semaphores, condition variables, monitors; producer-consumer, readers-writers, dining philosophers
Deadlock: conditions, resource allocation graphs, prevention, avoidance (banker's algorithm), detection and recovery
Concurrency bugs: atomicity and order violations; lock-free structures in brief
Inter-process communication: shared memory, message passing, pipes, sockets

units.title: Memory management
topics: Address spaces, address binding, logical versus physical addresses; base and bounds
Contiguous allocation and fragmentation; segmentation; free-space management (first fit, best fit, buddy, slab)
Paging: page tables, TLBs, multi-level and inverted page tables; address translation worked examples
Virtual memory: demand paging, page faults, copy-on-write; replacement (FIFO, LRU, clock, optimal); thrashing and the working set
Memory in xv6: page tables, allocation, implementing lazy allocation

units.title: File systems
topics: Files, directories, links, permissions; the file system interface and the VFS layer
Storage layout: inodes, extents, bitmaps, directories; FAT, ext4, NTFS compared
Crash consistency: fsck, journaling, copy-on-write (ZFS, Btrfs), log-structured file systems
Caching, buffering, read-ahead; disk scheduling (FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN); SSDs and flash translation layers
RAID and reliability; network file systems

units.title: I/O system
topics: I/O hardware: controllers, ports, buses, polling, interrupts, DMA
The I/O subsystem: device drivers, character and block devices, buffering, spooling
Writing a simple device driver; interrupt handling in the kernel
Clocks, timers and power management

units.title: Protection, security and virtual machines
topics: Protection domains, access control lists, capabilities; user authentication and privilege
OS security: buffer overflows, privilege escalation, sandboxing, address-space randomisation
Virtual machines: hypervisors (type 1 and 2), trap-and-emulate, paravirtualisation, hardware support, nested page tables
Containers: namespaces, cgroups, images; VMs versus containers

units.title: Multiple processor systems and mobile operating systems
topics: Multiprocessor scheduling, load balancing, processor affinity, cache coherence effects, NUMA
Distributed and cluster operating systems in brief
Mobile operating systems: Android architecture (Linux kernel, ART, Binder, app sandbox), iOS; power management, app life cycle, permissions
Case study: the Linux kernel and how to contribute; the future of operating systems
